# Independent audit: coherent nonaffine middle translation

Source: `candidate c4c8ccba329fa548`.

**Result: PASS, all four sections.** The source verifier passes 159 exact
checks. No repair is needed. The result is local around the stated
strictly compatible symmetric-endpoint baseline and does not assert
smoothing of arbitrary nonaffine centroid graphs.

## 1. Exact actual bodies and all-source attainment

The inclusion rho*T subset epsilon*h+c*T is equivalent to
-epsilon*h in (c-rho)T by the supporting inequalities of the homothetic
triangle. Since c>rho and zero is interior to T, it holds for both
signs of all sufficiently small epsilon. Endpoint fibers are exposed;
every convex combination at base zero has equal endpoint weights and
its endpoint component in rho*T. Thus the convex hull has exactly the
three displayed integer fibers, positive area in each, full ambient
interior, and constant total mixed area (9/2)R.

At the centered baseline, the previously audited exact three-triangle
theorem gives depth 2R, with only three canonical normals and zero tilt.
The both-proper endpoint value 4rho^2 is strictly below its saturation
plateau (9/2)rho^2, so the integer tilt minimizer is unique. A nonzero
middle point has a positive coordinate in one canonical normal; shifting
that cap through the point loses positive middle area and gains no other
area. This proves unique baseline global optimality, with endpoint
maxima exactly 2rho^2 and a strict gap.

For a bounded source neighborhood and small epsilon, continuous normals
can be unit-normalized and integer tilt clamped at one common finite
bound, beyond which the endpoints are fully saturated. The own trace is
independent of this tilt, so the clamping preserves all actual traces.
Pure integer caps are strictly improved by a finite nonvertical cap that
keeps endpoint statuses and takes a proper subset of the own full fiber.
Continuous positive-area fibers make cap mass continuous on the resulting
compact parameter space, including supporting and vertex transitions.
The same bound works on the translated-back compact middle fibers, so
uniform convergence of depth follows. The uniqueness/localization and
separated endpoint arguments consequently use justified compactness.

## 2. Full cap charts and the true normal minimum

In the chart of the maximizing triangle vertex (2,-1), the other vertex
height gaps are 3r and 3(1-theta)r. The edge-intercept formula therefore
gives exactly equation (5) for both signs of sufficiently small theta.
All traces remain strictly inside the one-vertex chamber near baseline.
The two equal endpoint numerators differ only by plus/minus alpha;
therefore alpha=0 is their unique exact minimizing tilt throughout the
local chart, not merely to first order.

At baseline the full normal Hessian is diag(2,R), with zero cross term.
The angular factor is (2-theta)^2/[2(1-theta)], whose second derivative
at zero is one. This verifies the entry R and the positive definite
normal minimum. Uniform positive definiteness on small convex charts
and the implicit-function theorem give unique smooth branch minima.
Vertex permutations are continuous-coordinate symmetries of determinant
absolute value one and leave the integer base unchanged.

The compact complement of the three isolated baseline menu directions
has a positive gap; uniform cap continuity preserves it. Hence every
actual nearby global minimizing normal lies in one of these charts and
the true raw depth is the minimum of their three optimized branch values.
Saturated and opposite/noncanonical directions have genuinely been
excluded by the gap. Pure integer caps were separately dominated.

## 3. Reoptimized source is unique and actual

The baseline source gradients are -2W times the three canonical normals.
The gradients of the two branch differences are independent. Their
implicit intersection therefore defines a unique smooth nearby source
where all three values agree. A spanning positive dependence of the
three source gradients persists under small perturbations; compactness
of the unit circle gives the uniform negative directional margin stated
in the source. With uniformly bounded second derivatives, at least one
branch strictly decreases along every sufficiently small nonzero source
displacement. Thus the intersection is a strict local maximum of the
TRUE all-normal depth, not merely a stationary cap average.

Depth superlevel sets in the middle plane are convex. If another middle
point had depth at least this local maximum, the segment to it would
contradict the strict local maximum. This proves unique global middle
optimality. The fixed endpoint depth gap then proves unique global mixed
optimality. The selected point remains interior to the displayed middle
fiber by continuity from its baseline interior position.

At that source all three chart minima are critical and are the complete
menu. Their source gradients are negative positive section masses times
their actual continuous normals, so their positive circuit is genuine.
All three integer tilts are exactly zero by the endpoint symmetry, as
claimed. No unproved continuous choice of a distant minimizer is used.

## 4. Coherent derivatives and exact coefficient

The first branch variation is 2u_i.(c*h-W*y1). Equality of the three
branch values and the zero sum of their spanning normals force the
common first coefficient to vanish and y1=(c/W)h. The three first center
relative displacements then satisfy sum r_z*delta_z=0 and
sum delta_z delta_z^T=D h h^T, with
D=2lambda^2+(1-lambda)^2=2R/W^2.

Writing a general relative displacement as (d1,d2), direct differentiation
of one cap summand at theta=alpha=0 gives

    r(d1+2d2)+(1/2)d1(d1+2d2).

Thus the angular first-order forcing vanishes for precisely the same
weighted vector balance, and every optimized angular derivative at zero
is zero. Positive normal Hessian R then gives theta_i=O(epsilon^2).
Consequently optimizing normals causes no second-order value correction;
this is proved after reoptimizing the source, not assumed by freezing it.

The canonical second coefficient is
-2W*u_i.y2+(D/2)(u_i.h)^2. Summing the three equal coefficients yields
q2=D(h1^2+h1*h2+h2^2)/3, and the two coordinate equations give exactly
the stated y2. The quadratic is positive definite; therefore for h!=0,
Q(epsilon)-2R has positive leading coefficient epsilon^2*q2 on BOTH
sides of zero. Smoothness supplies the O(epsilon^3) remainder. The mass
is unchanged, so the local normalized-depth sign is also correct.

The proof does not extend this sign to a finite displacement, the
midpoint-contact boundary c=rho, unequal endpoints, or arbitrary centroid
graphs. These scope qualifications remain necessary and are stated.
